inspiration: Creature row as data: one line per NPC carries scale band (min and max), hue, attack speed, movement speed, aggressive and assist radius, a death-blow flag and up to three loot tables with their own chances (serverdata/npc/npc_1.sdb line 1 header and line 3 creature row). Recreate the schema for our creature catalogue with our own numbers.

Scale band for variety from one model: a creature's scale is a min-max range (0.6 to 0.8 in the sample row), so one body gives several sizes at a glance. Keep the band idea, change the species and proportions (npc_1.sdb line 3).

Trap family as a small table: each type has a detonate range below the blast radius, a damage range with min and max, a damage type and one explosion effect file. Four to six types cover hazard variety (serverdata/combat/mine_types.sdb lines 3-6).

Spawn pulse near a player: a percentage roll on movement, a cap on alive spawns near the player (default 12), an egg placed within 250 metres, and one elite plus normal slots 1 to 4 drawn from a spawn set (DynamicSpawnService.kt lines 58-59, 98-100, 149-170, 198). Map onto walk density; move the cap to zone data.

Three-tier loot roll: up to three tables per NPC, each with its own chance, and a chance of zero or less means the table does not exist; credits and items toggled separately (LootGenerationService.kt lines 98-109, 124, 77). Keep the three-tier idea for our loot ceremony.
Difficulty tiers inside one loot id: normal, elite and boss rows share an id and a level band (serverdata/loot/loot_table.sdb header and first rows). Pattern for elite and boss loot in one table.

Syllable grammar for names: a vowel set, start and end consonant sets, a max length and a surname chance, one grammar file for each species (src/main/resources/namegen/resources.txt). Build our own grammar per faction; do not copy the donor lists.

briefs.label: Plated pack-hunter (category: large melee beast)
briefs.why: A big plated animal that attacks slowly and moves fast reads as a threat at range and rewards dodging.
briefs.keep: scale band with a wide size range; attack speed slower than move speed; aggressive radius and assist radius set separately so the pack calls in
briefs.change: our own limb count and head shape; a palette built from one new hue family; a different hide pattern and an ember glow at the seams
briefs.ref: serverdata/npc/npc_1.sdb line 3 (creature row; read the numbers, not the name)

briefs.label: Proximity trap family
briefs.why: A small set of traps with clear detonate ranges and damage bands gives hazards variety at 375 wide.
briefs.keep: detonate range smaller than blast radius; damage min and max per type; one damage type and one effect per trap
briefs.change: our trap shapes and names; spike, sigil and rune types instead of mines; our own effect files

briefs.label: Walk-density spawn pulse
briefs.why: A small percent chance per step with a cap on nearby spawns keeps the world busy but never crowded.
briefs.keep: percent roll on movement; alive cap near the player; spawn point offset within a set distance; one elite and normal slots per set
briefs.change: a round offset instead of a square; cap per zone rather than per player; a visible rising signal before the spawn appears

briefs.label: Three-tier loot roll
briefs.why: Three tables with their own chances let one kill give a common, a rare and a boss drop without one big table.
briefs.keep: three tables per creature; a chance of zero removes a table; credits and items switched separately
briefs.change: our item families and rarity colours; a drop ceremony sound per tier; no copied table

briefs.label: Syllable name grammar per faction
briefs.why: A short grammar with start and end sounds gives names that feel of one people without a list.
briefs.keep: vowel set; start and end consonant sets; a max length; a surname chance
briefs.change: our own sound palette per faction; no copied lists; a different length cap
